headline_drivers: Q2 2025 earnings beat and raise: EPS -$0.44 vs -$0.72 consensus (≈39% beat) and revenue $232.1M vs $211.3M consensus (≈10% beat), plus FY revenue growth guidance raised to 24–25% from 15–16% (Investing.com recap of Guardant Health Q2 2025 results, reported mid‑May 2025)

Re‑rating on growth/valuation debate: despite negative LTM free cash flow (~$229M), a Simply Wall St DCF analysis pegs intrinsic value at ~$173.89 vs ~$87.60 spot (≈50% upside), reinforcing a growth‑story multiple expansion alongside strong multi‑year share performance (Simply Wall St article, context over the last year)

Capital raise at premium valuation: upsized underwritten public offering of 3,333,333 shares at $90.00 per share, raising ≈$284.4M net, signaling institutional demand and strengthening balance sheet for continued growth investment (Guardant Health press release on stock offering pricing)
summary: The recent 20–30%+ surge in GH is being driven primarily by a classic "beat and raise" quarter that materially reset expectations: Q2 2025 revenue and EPS both came in well ahead of consensus while management sharply lifted full‑year revenue growth guidance from the mid‑teens to mid‑20s. That fundamental inflection has been reinforced by a bullish valuation narrative (DCF work suggesting substantial upside even after the run) and an upsized secondary offering successfully priced at $90, which together signal both institutional demand and confidence in Guardant’s long‑term growth trajectory. With the stock breaking to 52‑week highs on these catalysts, a layer of technical/ momentum buying is likely adding to the move, but the core driver is a growth and sentiment re‑rating off a strong earnings beat and higher guide.
